Name: Over the Middle
Description: A read-based passing play where a middle receiver crosses between linebackers. Its strength lies in its ability to create confusion for interior defenders who must react to a crossing runner; however, it requires precise timing and a clear path from the offensive side.

Name: Halfback option
Description: This is a hybrid run/pass play where the back can choose to tuck the ball if the intended pass isn't open. The strength of this play is keeping the defense guessing about whether it will be a handoff or a pass; its weakness is the high level of split-second decision-making required from the running back.

Name: Four Verticals
Description: A high-risk, high-reward play where four receivers sprint deep to stretch the secondary to its limit. Its strength is creating maximum space and potential for large gains, while its weakness is a higher risk of interception if the pass is not perfectly executed.

Name: Smash
Description: This is a high-low concept that uses a short hitch and a deeper corner route to stress a single defender's coverage. The strength lies in creating conflict for the defender who must choose between two targets; its weakness is limited yardage if the pass isn't thrown quickly.

Name: Mesh
Description: This play features two receivers crossing in the middle at shallow depth to "rub off" defenders, making it difficult for defenders to maintain coverage. Its weakness is that it can be effectively countered by a disciplined zone defense.

Name: Slant-Flat
Description: Combining an outside slant with an inside flat route, this play specifically targets and attacks a zone defense. The strength of this play is forcing the defender to choose between two options at different angles, while its weakness lies in the requirement for perfect synchronization from both receivers.

Name: Sail
Description: This "pass flood" involves three levels—deep, intermediate, and short—on one side of the field. Its strength is overwhelming a specific area with multiple targets; however, its complexity makes it more difficult to execute flawlessly compared to simpler routes.

Name: Stick
Description: A quick-hit play where a receiver runs upfield then stops abruptly as a target for the quarterback. The strength is catching linebackers before they can react to the stop; its weakness is that it requires an extremely sharp and well-timed cut from the runner.

Name: Flea Flicker
Description: This deceptive play involves tossing a handoff back to the QB, who then throws a long pass behind a defense expecting a run. Its strength is catching the defense off guard with a sudden switch; its weakness is the time required for the ball transfer.

Name: Hail Mary
Description: A desperate, long-distance pass into the end zone during the final moments of a game. The strength is its high payoff as a last resort when no other options exist, while its weakness is a low completion rate and high risk of turnover.

Name: Hook and Lateral
Description: A receiver catches a hook and immediately pitches it to a trailing teammate.

Name: Power
Description: This is a physically intense play where a guard pulls across the line to lead block through a gap in the defense. Its strength is its effectiveness in short-yardage situations; however, it can be stopped if the defenders anticipate the guard's movement.

Name: Counter
Description: A misdirection play where the runner cuts back behind a pulling guard to catch the defense off balance. The strength lies in creating confusion at the point of attack, while its weakness is that any lack of timing from the offensive line exposes the ball carrier.

Name: Trap
Description: An interior run where an offensive lineman intentionally leaves a defender unblocked for a teammate to hit them from the side. Its strength is the massive gain created by isolating and hitting defenders on their "blind" side; its weakness is the high level of coordination required between blockers.

Name: Isolation
Description: This is a straightforward running play where a fullback blocks one linebacker 1-on-1, allowing the ball carrier to break through. The strength is simplicity and ease of execution; however, it can be easily stopped if the defense successfully manages the lead blocker.

Name: Inside Zone
Description: In this maneuver, the offensive line moves laterally as a single unit, which allows the running back to find an internal seam in the defensive front. Its strength is its reliability and consistency across many plays; however, it can be countered by an aggressive interior defense.

Name: Outside Zone
Description: The offensive line flows toward the sideline as a collective unit to open up the perimeter for the runner. Its strength is the ability to stretch the defense horizontally across the field; its weakness is its vulnerability to defenders who can successfully "contain" the ball.

Name: Pitch
Description: A wide play where the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back sprinting toward the sideline of the field. The strength is utilizing the runner's speed to cross the line of scrimmage quickly; however, since the ball is in motion during the handoff, it is more susceptible to being stripped.

Name: Sweep
Description: A perimeter play where the offensive line creates a moving wall to protect a runner heading toward the outside. The strength of this play is the protection provided by the linemen as they form a corridor; its weakness is that it requires a high level of engagement from the defense's edge players.

Name: Read Option
Description: This dynamic play involves the QB reading an edge defender

Name: Jet Sweep
Description: A high-speed play where a receiver in motion takes a pitch from the QB to strike the sideline. The strength is the momentum gained by the runner, which often confuses defenders; however, it requires perfect coordination between the QB and the moving receiver.

Name: Punt
Description: Used to move the ball away from the goal line when scoring isn't likely.

Name: Field goal
Description: A kick through the uprights used when the offense is near the goal line.
